newsitem.title: USA: Lobbyist indicted for gifts to former U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Lobbyist indicted for gifts to former U.S. official.

text.p: A federal grand jury has indicted lobbyist Richard Douglas on charges he gave illegal gifts to then-Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy and masterminded illegal political donations to Espy's brother, the independent counsel investigating the case announced on Wednesday.

The 19-count indictment also accused Douglas of "material false statements" to federal investigators and wire fraud in obtaining a mortgage. Douglas worked for Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, at the time of the alleged offences in 1993 and 1994 while Espy served in the cabinet.
Espy resigned in 1994 amid accusations he accepted illegal gifts and favours from companies he was supposed to regulate. He has repeatedly denied doing anything wrong.
Indictment of Douglas, a longtime friend of Espy, was announced by independent counsel Donald Smaltz, who was appointed two years ago to investigate Espy.

"This is yet another attempt to coerce someone into saying negative things about Mike Espy," said Reid Weingarten, Espy's lawyer. "One wonders how many decent honourable people like Richard Douglas will have to get hurt before the special prosecutor realises Mike Espy committed no crimes."

Sun-Diamond was convicted last month of violating federal law on charges dealing with the same gifts and donations cited against Douglas. James Lake, a partner in a Washington public relations firm, pleaded guilty this year to wire fraud and election law violation in the donations.

In its trial, Sun-Diamond argued that the gifts, which included lavish meals, luggage and tickets to the 1993 U.S. Open tennis tournament, were due to friendship and were not an attempt to sway Espy's judgment or win favourable policies.

Smaltz said the gifts were worth a total of $10,780 and the contributions to Henry Espy's campaign totalled $2,000. Charges involving the mortgage "were uncovered during the course" of investigating Espy, he said.

As a result of its conviction, Sun-Diamond has been barred from participating in all federal food purchase programmes for three years. The cooperative said this month it hoped to reverse the Agriculture Department decision.
